toolStatus: Opened in full: PressReader MOJO (Dinosaur Jr.), SLUG Magazine (Mogwai), Wikipedia Kevin Shields, Modern Girls (Snail Mail), 9:30 Club Tumblr (Snail Mail), FACT (Ride), Denver Westword via den-experimental.voicemediagroup.com mirror (Hook), 4th Estate Big Star page, Far Out (Cobain), Aaron Davis Music (Patterson Hood). web_fetch refused the Buddyhead archive URL (web.archive.org/web/20050408040110/http://www.buddyhead.com/music/kevinshields/) and the Line of Best Fit nine-songs Nastanovich URL because neither had appeared in a search result. joy-division>the-stooges.found: “He would say to me, ‘Listen to this record,’ and he gives me Metallic K.O. by the Stooges,” Hook recalls.
joy-division>the-stooges.citation: Peter Hook to Denver Westword (2 Sep 2022), on Ian Curtis educating him musically: "He would say to me, 'Listen to this record,' and he gives me Metallic K.O. by the Stooges."

new-order>the-stooges.note: The same Westword page (https://den-experimental.voicemediagroup.com/music/peter-hook-joy-division-new-order-14876858/) has Hook saying Curtis gave him Metallic K.O. in 1970s Manchester, before New Order existed. It supports Hook's own exposure, not New Order. The 'blew my mind' wording is not on the page. Proposal: keep the link on Joy Division only and remove New Order, or record it as 'reported' at most.

rem>big-star.note: Two searches plus a full read of https://www.4thestate.co.uk/products/big-star-the-story-of-rocks-forgotten-band-rob-jovanovic-9780007149087/. 'I was hoping we might get as popular as Big Star' was not found anywhere. The 4th Estate page carries a pull-quote attributed to Peter Buck, R.E.M., 1991: "I want to make an album of real genius, to sit alongside the Stones' 'Exile On Main Street', and Big Star's 'Third'". It is a publisher's blurb, not an interview page, so I did not mark it ok. Proposal: replace the caption with this quote as tier 'reported' if a blurb is acceptable; otherwise find Buck's original 1991 interview.

nirvana>ramones.found: The interviewer then mentioned the new wave genre, which Nirvana liked, saying, “The whole new wave concept, when it began, was very pop, I don’t know if you can name any bands (that influenced you),” to which Cobain responded, “The B-52’s, Devo, you know, anything… Ramones”.
nirvana>ramones.citation: Asked in a Rio de Janeiro interview (21 Jan 1993) which new wave bands influenced Nirvana, Kurt Cobain answered, as quoted by Far Out: "The B-52's, Devo, you know, anything… Ramones".

candidates.speaker: the-human-league
candidates.sentence: Ware began speaking about the early electronic scene in Sheffield emerging from the industrial noise of the city, meeting Ian Craig Marsh in a youth project called Meat Whistle and going to see Roxy Music at Sheffield University, with Brian Eno specifically influencing his interest in making music.

offMap.name: Spacemen 3
offMap.sentence: But from my point of view, we did definitely listen to all the bands around, and we were feeding that, so we were being influenced by, for example, Spacemen 3, feeding that back into a new song, and then releasing it.

offMap.name: Avril Lavigne
offMap.sentence: I can confidently say the artist who sparked my interest in music was Avril Lavigne (“I’m With You” is still the best song ever written) because she was an alt-rocker and sort of tomboy, which is what I always wanted to be when I was little (and she played a guitar).
